stories.title: Tenth Circuit Rules for NCAA in Wisne — Fifth Year Closed for Class of 2022

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text:
BREAKING: The Tenth Circuit reversed the nationwide injunction in Wisne v. NCAA.

The NCAA wins the 5-for-5 fight — for now.

~200 state cases still open. December portal opens in 13 days. Class of 2022 softball players must decide now. #CollegeSoftball

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
Tenth Circuit ruled for the NCAA in 5-for-5. What's next:

• En banc rehearing possible
• 200+ state court cases continue
• December portal opens Dec. 1
• Programs must finalize rosters NOW

Softball's most complicated offseason just got more complicated. #CollegeSoftball

facebook.long_form:
The legal fight over college softball's fifth-year eligibility just reached a major turning point.

The Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals reversed and vacated the nationwide preliminary injunction in *Wisne v. NCAA*, handing the NCAA a significant victory in the 5-for-5 eligibility litigation. The court found that the plaintiffs — class-of-2022 athletes who sought a fifth year of competition under COVID-era eligibility rules — failed to demonstrate a likelihood of success on their antitrust argument. Specifically, the panel rejected the plaintiffs' definition of the relevant labor market.

For softball players who had been counting on a fifth season, this ruling closes what many had considered the likeliest path to eligibility.

But the story isn't over. Approximately 200 concurrent lawsuits filed in state courts still involve up to 850 athletes across all sports, and a new 46-athlete group has already filed a fresh suit seeking an immediate preliminary injunction. Plaintiffs in the Wisne case can also petition for en banc rehearing from the full Tenth Circuit.

What does this mean for softball programs? The December transfer portal window opens in just 13 days (December 1–15). Programs that had budgeted roster spots for returning class-of-2022 players now need to reassess — and fast. The portal has become the primary relief valve.

We'll continue tracking this. The legal calendar is moving quickly.
facebook.image_caption: The Tenth Circuit ruled for the NCAA in the 5-for-5 case. Class-of-2022 softball players face a harder road to a fifth year. 200+ state cases remain. December portal opens December 1. #CollegeSoftball

stories.title: Oklahoma State Cowgirls Sign 7 on Signing Day — Five Four-Stars Join Stillwater

x_posts.label: Post 2
x_posts.text:
Oklahoma State signed SEVEN players on Signing Day, including five 4-star prospects.

Pitcher Ava Salcedo flipped from Grand Canyon to join the Cowgirls.

The Big 12 is wide open. #OKState #CowgirlSoftball

facebook.long_form:
Oklahoma State softball made a statement on National Signing Day.

The Cowgirls signed seven players, led by five four-star recruits. Among the highlights: pitcher Ava Salcedo flipped her commitment from Grand Canyon to join OSU's program in Stillwater. When a recruit changes course from another school to join your program, it says something about the direction you're heading.

Oklahoma State operates in an increasingly interesting landscape. With Oklahoma and Texas now in the SEC, the Big 12 has space at the top — and the Cowgirls are positioning themselves to claim it. A class this talent-dense signals that head coach Kenny Gajewski is serious about building a perennial contender.

For fans of the Cowgirls, Signing Day was a good day. Keep an eye on this program.

stories.title: FSU Softball Signs Highest-Rated Recruit in Program History — Five-Star Addison DeRoche

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
Florida State signed pitcher Addison DeRoche — No. 5 recruit nationally and the highest-rated prospect in FSU softball program history.

Plus 4-star catcher Layna Ayala. No. 13 class nationally.

The Noles are building. #FSUSoftball #Noles

facebook.long_form:
Florida State softball just shattered its own recruiting ceiling.

Pitcher Addison DeRoche — the No. 5 player nationally in the 2027 recruiting class — signed with the Seminoles on National Signing Day, becoming the highest-rated recruit in FSU softball program history. That's not a small thing. That's a program redefining what it's capable of attracting.

Signing day also brought four-star catcher Layna Ayala to Tallahassee, giving the Noles a talent infusion at two key positions. With the class ranked No. 13 nationally, FSU is building toward something.

DeRoche's addition addresses what has been an occasional vulnerability for the Seminoles: elite top-of-rotation pitching depth. Add in the transfer of Tennessee infielder Ella Dodge, and the 2027 Noles roster is starting to look like a team that can win a Super Regional.

Florida State hasn't won the Women's College World Series — but classes like this one are how programs get there.

stories.title: LSU Signs Portal Twins Pickens + Winchell to Complete No. 1 Class

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
LSU didn't stop at the No. 1 signing class.

Beth Torina added portal twins Mackenzie and Madison Pickens PLUS Notre Dame outfielder Michey Winchell to the 2027 roster.

No. 1 class. Targeted portal pieces. 2027 is loading. #LSUSoftball #GeauxTigers

facebook.long_form:
LSU's No. 1-ranked signing class is only part of the story.

After announcing the top-rated 2027 recruiting class in program history on November 11, coach Beth Torina went back to work. She signed portal twins Mackenzie and Madison Pickens — a rare simultaneous acquisition of sibling pitchers — and Notre Dame outfielder Michey Winchell, who will be a senior for the Tigers in 2027.

Winchell brings immediate starting experience from the ACC to a lineup that will need veteran leadership to surround its younger signees. The Pickens twins add pitching depth and rotation options.

What's emerging at LSU is a blueprint: sign the top high school class, add targeted portal pieces, manage outgoing transfers selectively rather than chasing every available name. The result is a 2027 roster that balances elite youth with proven experience.

The Women's College World Series in June 2027 is still far away. But if the Tigers can stay healthy and gel during the spring, Beth Torina is building a genuine championship contender.
facebook.image_caption: LSU added portal twins Mackenzie and Madison Pickens PLUS Notre Dame's Michey Winchell to their No. 1-ranked 2027 class. Beth Torina is building something special in Baton Rouge. #LSUSoftball #GeauxTigers

stories.title: Tennessee Returns 9 Starters — Lady Vols Fall Ball Points to SEC Title Contention

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
In a portal era that empties rosters every spring, Tennessee is returning NINE starters for 2027.

Sage Mardjetko (16-3, 1.26 ERA). Sophia Knight (.394 avg). Nine starters.

The Lady Vols are ready. #LadyVols #TennesseeSoftball

facebook.long_form:
Here's something you don't see every year in modern college softball: a program returning nine starters.

Tennessee is doing exactly that for 2027. After going 49-12 in 2026 with one of the best pitching staffs in the SEC, the Lady Vols are bringing back the core of that roster. NFCA First Team All-American Sage Mardjetko (16-3, 1.26 ERA, 171 strikeouts) returns as one of the premier pitchers in the country. Sophia Knight, who hit .394 as the team's leading hitter, also returns.

In an era when transfer portals empty lineups across the country every spring, returning nine starters is extraordinary continuity. It means Tennessee doesn't have to rebuild chemistry — they just have to execute.

The Lady Vols are legitimate SEC title contenders alongside Alabama, LSU, and OU. Their challenge in 2027 will be doing what Tennessee-caliber talent demands: reaching Tallahassee and competing for a national title.

Sage Mardjetko. Sophia Knight. Nine starters. The Lady Vols are ready.
